title: Introduce prefetch cohort simulator and alert smoothing
author: Priya Khandelwal
release_notes: Adds a deterministic prefetch cohort simulator for offline tuning, new cohort-level prefetch efficacy metrics and a dashboard; introduces per-cohort alert smoothing to reduce churn from seasonal prefetch variance.
description: Motivation: We continue to see noisy SLO alerts driven by prefetch warmup oscillations and seasonality in traffic shape. Teams tuning prefetch/autotune policies currently rely on ad-hoc synthetic runs or live canaries which produce noisy signals. This PR introduces: 1) a prefetch cohort simulator (deterministic synthetic runner) that can replay sampled traffic and exercise prefetch policies under controlled seeds; 2) cohort-level metrics and rollups (prefetch_hit_ratio_by_cohort, prefetch_efficacy_confidence, cohort_latency_seasonality_index) to measure effectiveness and detect seasonal variance; 3) an alert smoothing layer that operates on cohort rollups to reduce alert churn while preserving signal for real regressions; 4) a Redwood Console dashboard with simulator controls, cohort heatmaps, and a guided troubleshooting panel. Scope: telemetry ingestion changes (metrics + tags), a small simulation binary, dashboard JSON, unit + e2e tests for simulator determinism, and a migration that backfills cohort labels for 7 days for consistency. Checklist: - [x] Implement simulator engine and deterministic seed mode - [x] Emit cohort-level metrics with stable labels - [x] Add smoothing operator with config knobs (window, alpha, suppression-threshold) - [x] Console dashboard and runbook links - [x] Unit tests for simulator determinism - [x] E2E synthetic replay test against staging ingest - [x] Docs in telemetry/README describing how to run and interpret results Changeset summary: commits include simulator implementation, metrics schema changes, smoothing operator, dashboard, tests, docs, and small CI pipeline tweaks to run the simulator in a lightweight mode. Backwards compatibility: metric names are additive; smoothing operator is opt-in per-alert via config; dashboard is additive. Migration: a short backfill pipeline (run-once) that tags invocations into cohorts for the past 7 days so historical dashboards display cohort distributions. Why this design: simulator + cohort metrics let us evaluate policy changes offline and produce stable inputs to the alert-smoothing layer. The smoothing layer reduces noisy alert churn from predictable seasonal patterns (e.g., daytime prefetch bursts) while still surfacing persistent cost/latency regressions. Rollout plan: staged feature-flag rollout: - feature off in prod by default - enable simulator in staging for 24 hours to validate deterministic runs - enable cohort metrics ingestion on a small tenant slice for 48 hours - opt-in smoothing for low-sensitivity alerts and observe false positive rate for 7 days - full rollout if FPR drops >30% without missing latency regressions Documentation and runbooks included in this PR. Links: Linear tasks ENG-2345 (simulator), ENG-2390 (smoothing operator).

review_thread:
Ethan Morales: Can we guarantee simulator determinism across Go versions and minor dependency bumps?
Priya: Simulator uses a single RNG seed derived from an explicit seed param and pins internal scheduling; added a determinism test that runs across go1.20 and go1.21 in CI-lite. Also documented caveats in README.
Liang Wu: The smoothing operator could mask real regressions if configured too aggressively; can we expose an emergency bypass?
Priya: Yes — smoothing is opt-in at the alert rule level and includes a bypass flag that runs strict evaluation if an anomaly delta exceeds a configured escalation threshold. Added e2e test that validates bypass behavior.
Sofia Ramos: Need perf numbers — what's the extra cost of the smoothing operator at ingestion-time?
Priya: Measured at 100k events/s the smoothing operator adds ~6% CPU in our runner and ~2% memory; added a small benchmark in tests and an ops note.
Ethan: Approving pending one nit.
Priya: Addressed nit (renamed config key to smoothing_window_ms).
Liang: Approved.
Merge: squash and merge by Priya on 2026-02-28.
notes_for_ops: Operator config lives in telemetry/operators/config.yaml with defaults: smoothing_window_ms: 60000, alpha: 0.3, suppression_threshold: 0.15. Backfill job must be executed once in staging then prod; estimate 15m per 1M invocations. Dashboard includes a simulator control panel (seed, replay duration) — Ops can use this to reproduce tenant regressions deterministically.
benchmarks: Local benchmark harness included: sim-runner achieves ~3500 replays/s for 1-second traces on a c5.large-like instance; smoothing operator adds 6% CPU at 100k events/s on our perf-canary cluster.
how_to_validate: 1) Run telemetry/simulator with deterministic seed and compare output hash against known-good in tests/fixtures. 2) Deploy cohort metrics to staging and verify dashboard population. 3) Enable smoothing opt-in on a single low-sensitivity alert and observe alert rate over 7 days; compare false positive rate before/after. 4) Run backfill migration in staging and confirm no label collisions.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: smoothing can delay detection of fast regressions. Mitigation: bypass for large anomalies; opt-in rollout; canary tenant slice; clear runbook to disable smoothing per-alert quickly.
